rows.description: A young adult finds purpose not in a sudden vision but by committing to a craft, a person or a cause and staying long enough to feel it matter. Meaning often follows action.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: After loss, illness or failure, a person slowly builds a story in which the pain teaches or changes something. Forced silver linings feel false, but meaning found in one's own time can heal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person sees a friend find purpose in a path they themselves would not choose, such as devotion, farming or family. Respecting different sources of meaning avoids the urge to correct.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child giggles at funny faces, wrong words and sudden surprises. Early humour is about incongruity and safety, and laughing together bonds a child to a caregiver.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, playfulness, surprise, trust

rows.description: A child repeats the same joke ten times and finds bodily humour hilarious. Testing jokes teaches timing and audience, and groans from listeners are useful feedback.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child whose mistake becomes the class joke smiles outwardly while shrinking inside. Laughing along can be a survival tactic, not a sign the joke was harmless.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager uses sarcasm, memes and inside jokes to bond with peers. Shared humour signals who is in the group, and it can also be used to exclude others.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A team facing a crisis uses a well-timed joke to release tension and then returns to work. Humour helps when it includes everyone and lands after the problem is respected.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.subtype: Reading whether it is the time [Observer]
rows.description: A person notices that a joke at a funeral or during someone's fresh failure would wound and holds it. Timing and audience matter more than the joke itself.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child who spilled milk hides and says I am bad. Young children treat errors as identity, and an adult saying you made a mistake, you are not a mistake gives a first template of self-forgiveness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
